titleEn: If It Falls, Plant It Again!

pages.text: "I'll plant my own row!" Dingding stood barefoot in the planting paddy, holding a young rice plant. Dingding wanted a straight row like Grandma's. Water lapped around their ankles.
Dingding pushed the plant into the soil and let go. But it slowly leaned over on its side. "Why did it fall?" Dingding's hand stopped in midair.
Dingding planted it again, but it fell again. "It falls every time! I quit!" Dingding tossed the plant into the water and sat heavily on the bank. The floating plant drifted toward the lower paddy.
Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, splashed over from the next row. "When I was little, I must have let a hundred plants fall in this paddy." She took Dingding's hand and helped them up.
Grandma gave Dingding a young plant and explained softly. "Put the roots two finger joints deep into the soil. Then press the soil beside them gently." Dingding nodded.

Back in the paddy, Dingding pushed the roots deep and pressed the soil gently. When Dingding let go, the rice plant stood straight! It stood on the third try. "It stood! If It Falls, Plant It Again!" Dingding raised both hands.
The next plant fell over. But Dingding did not throw it. "That's all right. If It Falls, Plant It Again!" Dingding pushed the roots deeper and pressed the soil. The plant stood straight.

Mom retrieved the drifting plant from the lower paddy and came up the bank. "You threw this, didn't you?" Dingding sniffed its fresh grassy smell. "I'll plant that one again, too!" Dingding reached out.
Dingding planted the last plant. "One, roots two finger joints deep! Two, press the soil beside them gently! Three, if it falls, plant it again!" Dingding's row stood straight beside Grandma's.

Mom and Grandma hugged Dingding from both sides. "Your row is the straightest!" Even if a plant did not stand the first time, trying again helped it stand little by little. Dingding pointed to their row. "If It Falls, Plant It Again!"
